To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the attitudes and values of the staff in a multidisciplinary cancer care team did not change over the course of a prospective study.

1) the attitudes and values of a group of staff members involved in the care and research of patients with advanced lung cancer were studied over an eighteen-month period; 2) there were no significant differences between the values and attitudes of the staff at the beginning and at the end of the study; 3) the values and attitudes were consistent with the values and attitudes reported in the literature.
There is little relationship between staff attitudes and values and the amount of time they spend in contact with patients with cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model of the multidisciplinary cancer care team which can be used as an educational tool for health care professionals and as a basis for the design of a cancer care team for patients with cancer and their families.
the identification of the values of the staff members in the care of cancer patients.
the attitudes of the multidisciplinary team toward the care of patients and families with cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the attitudes and values of this multidisciplinary staff team did not change during the period of the study.
there were no changes in staff attitudes or values over the course of the study.
the staff attitudes and values did not change over the period of study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the attitudes and values of staff involved in the care for cancer patients do not appear to change significantly over a period of seventeen months despite increased exposure to patients with advanced cancer.
staff members who work in cancer care are a unique group of professionals.
the staff attitudes and values did not appear to influence the quality of care provided to our patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
staff attitudes and values are not easily changed.

the attitudes and values of cancer care team members are stable and that the attitudes and beliefs about life, disease and illness of cancer care team staff members are similar to those of the general population.
it is possible to study the attitudes and values of a cancer care team over time and to demonstrate the stability of these values and attitudes.
